summary: Service worker rescans the entire dynamic-route registration table (IndexedDB) on every GET request
description:
Background
The OMRS service worker's default request handler (esm-app-shell/src/service-worker/routing.ts) determines the caching strategy for every GET request. When a request carries no x-omrs-offline-caching-strategy header, it falls back to getHandlerKeyFromDynamicRouteRegistrations, which on every request:
opens a fresh ServiceWorkerDb (Dexie/IndexedDB) connection,

reads the entire dynamicRouteRegistrations table via .toArray(), and

compiles and tests a fresh new RegExp(route.pattern) against the URL for every registration.

This cost is negligible when the table is empty, but the table grows once offline mode is enabled and patients are synced — each synced patient (and its clinical data) registers dynamic routes. As a result, every un-headered GET — including live patient search and each paginated page — pays an IndexedDB open + full table scan + N regex compilations before the request is even dispatched. This is client-side overhead unrelated to network reachability, so it degrades performance even when the backend is on a fast LAN.
Requested change
Reduce the per-request cost of dynamic-route lookup in the service worker so it does not scale linearly with the number of registered offline routes on every request. Options include caching the registration list in memory (invalidated on registerDynamicRoute / clearDynamicRoutes messages), reusing a single ServiceWorkerDb/Dexie connection instead of constructing one per request, and precompiling the route regexes. Behavior of route matching and caching strategies must remain unchanged.
Acceptance criteria
The dynamic-route registration data and its compiled regexes are not re-read/re-compiled from IndexedDB on every GET request; repeated requests reuse cached state.

Cached state is correctly invalidated when routes are registered or cleared, so route matching stays correct after offline sync changes.

No change to which strategy a given URL resolves to (existing routing behavior preserved).

Automated tests in esm-app-shell covering: strategy resolution still matches the same routes after the optimization, cache invalidation on registerDynamicRoute/clearDynamicRoutes, and that a request with many registered routes does not trigger a full per-request table rescan.
